newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada guarantees funding for global broadcasts.
newsitem.headline: Canada guarantees funding for global broadcasts.

text.p: The Canadian government pledged on Monday to continue funding for Radio Canada International, Canada's international broadcasting service.
"We are guaranteeing that Canada's broadcasting voice will continue to be heard around the world," Heritage Minister Sheila Copps said in a statement.

The federal government temporarily rescued Radio Canada International last December after the service's parent, the Canadian Broadcasting Corp., announced it would close the operation because of a lack of funding.

Ottawa initally pledged just one year of funding, but today's announcement secures an annual C$15.52 million a year beginning in 1998-99 from the government. The money will come from funds set aside in the 1997 federal budget.

"With its funding now secure, I believe that RCI can better plan for the future, adapt to the exciting advancements in communications technologies, and thus become an integral element of Canada's international information strategy," Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said in a statement.

RCI broadcasts to Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, the United States, Asia and the Caribbean through shortwave radio and satellite and through partnerships with local foreign broadcasters.
